title: tcspecial simulator configuration
description:
What tcssim needs in order to stand in for the payloads of a tcspecial configuration: how fast each one sends, and what it does wrong. Nothing here describes a payload -- the configuration does that, and the two are joined by name.

A setting written with nothing after it is a setting not stated, which is what the editor writes into the form it makes: every payload of the configuration and every setting a payload may state, so that a reader can see what there is to answer.

tcssim.description: What tcssim itself is told. Required: tcssim does not start without it, and a harness cannot wait for a simulator without knowing where to ask.

ready.description: The UDP address, as address:port, at which tcssim answers whether it has made its stand-ins. One no other run uses: a simulator left running holds it, and a second one started on the same address is refused.

thermostat.description: The hysteresis nodes of the configuration tcssim stands in for, one name or several separated by commas, as a vehicle of several zones, or a staged thermostat, has several: for each it reads the simulated sensors whose data reaches that node and switches the simulated heaters the node's data reaches, with the node's setpoint and band, so the loop closes with no tcspecial running. A name blank between commas, or written twice, is refused, and so are two of them switching one heater. Never with tcspecial running, whose own thermostat switches the same heaters.

seed.description: What the simulation's random numbers start from, so that a run's noise can be had again. Unstated is a seed of tcssim's choosing, which it reports as it starts.

world.description: The world the simulated payloads are joined to: the temperature its surroundings are about, and its physics. YAML only: a simulator file written in XML has none.

ambient_temp.description: The temperature every thermal mass's surroundings are about, written with its unit: `288.15 K`. One for the world, every zone being in the one set of surroundings; each zone says how they vary about it with its swing and its wander. Required where there is a thermal mass.

physics.description: The vehicle's physical components, which the stand-ins measure and act on, and how they are joined. Each component is a part simulated alone, with fixed terminals of its type's; a connection joins an output to an input of the same kind. A stand-in joins a terminal with connects: component.terminal. Every figure is written with its unit.

components.description: The components, grouped by type: each entry is one key, `type` and the type, whose value is the list of that type's components, each named by its first key, `component: <name>`. The type decides a component's terminals and what else it states. The order of the types, and of the components of one, means nothing.

connections.description: How the components are joined, each from an output to an input of the same kind. An input that takes one output may be given one; a zone's heat takes the sum of every heater's. The order means nothing.

from.description: An output, as the component's name and the terminal's joined by a dot: `heater_1.heat`.

to.description: An input, written as from is: `zone.heat`.

simulated_payload_groups.description: Settings shared by the payloads that name them, each group named by its first key, `group: <name>`. A group says no type: a payload's type is the type it is written under.

simulate.description: Whether the payloads that name this group are simulated: true for tcssim to stand in for them, false for the real devices. A payload in a group that states it does not state it too.

group.description: The group's name, which a simulated payload names with group: to take its settings from it. An entry is named by this, its first key.

protocol.description: Which transport, for a network payload: udp, tcp or unix.

payload_address.description: Where the stand-in answers from, where it has an address of its own to bind.

packet_interval.description: How often it sends, as a length of time -- 1 s, 500 ms -- or the word `continuous` for as fast as the payload can be driven. Nought is no length of time and is refused, being the one value a file arrives at by accident. For a payload that sends on its own: one the configuration gives a trigger is asked instead, at the interval of the payload group it is in, so it states none here and there is nothing for an interval to mean.

segment_interval.description: How often a segment of a packet goes, as a length of time or the word `continuous`; defaults to the packet interval.

drop_percent.description: How often a packet is thrown away.

jitter.description: How late a packet may be, as a length of time, chosen afresh for each one and waited out inside the interval. A length of time and nothing else: leave it out for no jitter.

silent_after.description: How many packets before it stops talking.

close_after.description: How many before it hangs up, where it has a connection to hang up.

ignore_trigger_percent.description: How often it does not answer when it is asked.

connects.description: The terminal of the physics model this stand-in is joined to, as the component's name and the terminal's joined by a dot: `zone.temperature`, `heater_1.on`. Joined to an output, it reports it, in the encoding the conversion -- `to_kelvin` or `to_value` -- its readings go to expects, so the format, the scale and the offset are taken from that node and not stated here. A decision output is sent as `1` or `0`, at once when it changes and again every packet interval. Joined to an input, it drives it with what the vehicle sends -- a decision, or a value in the input's unit -- and sends nothing, being driven the whole of what it is for; its packet interval is how often it looks for what the vehicle sent.

offset.description: How far the place a reporting stand-in is on sits from what its terminal says, in the terminal's unit: `+0.2 K`. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

noise.description: A sensor's random error on each reading: the standard deviation, in its terminal's unit, of the normally distributed noise its electronics add: `0.03 K`. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

accuracy.description: The most a sensor's calibration is off by, in its terminal's unit, as its datasheet's accuracy: `0.5 K`. A fixed error is drawn once a run, normally distributed with a third of this as its standard deviation and never past it. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

drift.description: How far a sensor's error wanders, slowly: the standard deviation, in its terminal's unit, of an error drawn back towards nought with `drift_time` as its time constant. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

drift_time.description: How slowly a sensor's drift wanders, as a length of time. Required with `drift` and refused without it.

lag.description: A sensor's own time constant, as a length of time: how far behind the body it is on it follows. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

simulated_payloads.description: The payloads tcssim stands in for, grouped by type: each entry is one key, `type` and the type, whose value is the list of that type's simulated payloads, each named by its first key, `payload: <name>`. The type is the kind of payload it stands in for, the type the configuration writes that payload under: one of the interfaces a payload is reached over, a payload that is a program being the program itself and needing no stand-in. Said here as well as in the configuration so that a simulator file paired with the wrong configuration is caught rather than simulating the wrong thing.

tcsgui.description: What the editor arranged: where each physics component of the world was drawn. Last in the file and in a section of its own, because the sections above say what tcssim stands in for and this says where somebody put the boxes on a screen; tcssim ignores it. A component named here and not in the world is a position left behind, and kept; a component named nowhere here is laid out by the editor. Each entry names the component it is about by its first key, `node: <name>`, as a configuration's tcsgui section names its nodes.

node.description: The physics component this is about, as its `component:` names it.

simulatedType.description: The key of an entry of simulated_payloads: the word type, a space, and a kind of payload.

simulate.description: Whether this payload is simulated: true for tcssim to stand in for it, false for the real device. Required, from this payload or from its group, and not from both: a payload does not override its group's. Empty is not stated.

payload.description: The payload of the configuration this stands in for, by its name: the two files are joined by it. An entry is named by this, its first key.

group.description: A group whose settings this payload takes for whatever it does not state itself.

protocol.description: Which transport, for a network payload: udp, tcp or unix.

payload_address.description: Where the stand-in answers from, where it has an address of its own to bind.

packet_interval.description: How often it sends, as a length of time or the word `continuous` for as fast as the payload can be driven; a triggered payload states none, there being nothing for an interval to mean.

segment_interval.description: How often a segment of a packet goes, as a length of time or the word `continuous`; defaults to the packet interval.

drop_percent.description: How often a packet is thrown away.

jitter.description: How late a packet may be, as a length of time, chosen afresh for each one and waited out inside the interval. A length of time and nothing else: leave it out for no jitter.

silent_after.description: How many packets before it stops talking.

close_after.description: How many before it hangs up, where it has a connection to hang up.

ignore_trigger_percent.description: How often it does not answer when it is asked.

connects.description: The terminal of the physics model this stand-in is joined to, as the component's name and the terminal's joined by a dot: `zone.temperature`, `heater_1.on`. Joined to an output, it reports it, in the encoding the conversion -- `to_kelvin` or `to_value` -- its readings go to expects, so the format, the scale and the offset are taken from that node and not stated here. A decision output is sent as `1` or `0`, at once when it changes and again every packet interval. Joined to an input, it drives it with what the vehicle sends -- a decision, or a value in the input's unit -- and sends nothing, being driven the whole of what it is for; its packet interval is how often it looks for what the vehicle sent.

offset.description: How far the place a reporting stand-in is on sits from what its terminal says, in the terminal's unit: `+0.2 K`. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

noise.description: A sensor's random error on each reading: the standard deviation, in its terminal's unit, of the normally distributed noise its electronics add: `0.03 K`. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

accuracy.description: The most a sensor's calibration is off by, in its terminal's unit, as its datasheet's accuracy: `0.5 K`. A fixed error is drawn once a run, normally distributed with a third of this as its standard deviation and never past it. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

drift.description: How far a sensor's error wanders, slowly: the standard deviation, in its terminal's unit, of an error drawn back towards nought with `drift_time` as its time constant. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

drift_time.description: How slowly a sensor's drift wanders, as a length of time. Required with `drift` and refused without it.

lag.description: A sensor's own time constant, as a length of time: how far behind the body it is on it follows. With `connects` to an output and refused otherwise.

heater.description: A heater: a resistance on a supply, switched on and off. Its terminals are on, an input driven by a decision; heat, in W; and current, in A. Its on must be joined to a stand-in the vehicle drives.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

power.description: What it gives out while on at its nominal voltage, written with its unit: `60 W`.

voltage.description: Its supply's nominal voltage, written with its unit: `28 V`. With its power, says what current it draws.

ripple.description: How far its supply's voltage wanders, as a fraction of nominal: the standard deviation, written bare. Its power goes as the square of its voltage and its current as the voltage.

ripple_time.description: How slowly its supply wanders, as a length of time. Required with `ripple` and refused without it.

thermal_mass.description: A thermal mass: one body at one temperature, which cools towards its surroundings, the world's ambient_temp, and is warmed by the heat joined to it. It starts at ambient_temp unless `start` says otherwise, because a vehicle coming up cold is the case a thermostat exists for. Its terminals are heat, in W, the sum of every heater's joined to it; and temperature, in K.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

time_constant.description: How fast it loses the difference between itself and its surroundings, as a length of time: after one of these it has lost all but 1/e of it.

capacity.description: How much heat it takes to warm it a kelvin, written with its unit: `20 J/K`. What turns a heater's watts into kelvin a second.

swing.description: How far its surroundings swing either side of the world's ambient_temp, written with its unit, as a sine wave: a day and a night, or an orbit's sun and shadow.

period.description: How long one swing takes, as a length of time. Required with `swing` and refused without it.

wander.description: How far its surroundings wander at random, written with its unit: the standard deviation of a departure drawn back towards nought with `wander_time` as its time constant.

wander_time.description: How slowly its surroundings wander, as a length of time. Required with `wander` and refused without it.

start.description: Where it starts, written with its unit: `292.15 K`. Left out, it starts at its surroundings, the world's ambient_temp.

sun.description: The sun: its terminal is light, a ratio, one in sunlight and nought in shadow. Each change is an event, foreseen from the orbit.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

period.description: How long one orbit takes, as a length of time: `90 min`.

eclipse.description: How much of an orbit is in shadow, as a fraction, written bare: `0.35`. From nought up to but not one.

start.description: How far round the orbit it starts, from the start of its sunlight, as a fraction, written bare. Unstated is nought.

solar_array.description: A solar array: its terminals are light, an input taking a ratio, which must be joined; and current, in A, its full-sun current times the light.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

current.description: What it gives in full sunlight, written with its unit: `7 A`.

load.description: A load: its terminals are shed, a decision, shedding it while asserted and never where nothing is joined; and current, in A, nought while shed.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

current.description: What it draws while it is on, written with its unit: `2 A`.

bus.description: A power bus: its terminals are supply and demand, in A, each the sum of what is joined to it, and current, in A, supply less demand. It has no settings.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

battery.description: A battery: its terminals are offered, in A, what the bus has left over, which must be joined; voltage, in V; current, in A, what flows in, nought into a full battery; and charge, a ratio. Reaching full or empty is an event, foreseen.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

capacity.description: How much charge it holds full, written with its unit: `10 Ah`.

empty.description: Its open-circuit voltage empty, written with its unit: `24 V`.

full.description: Its open-circuit voltage full, more than empty: `33.2 V`.

resistance.description: Its internal resistance, written with its unit: `0.05 ohm`.

charge.description: How full it starts, as a fraction of its capacity, written bare: `0.6`.

engine.description: An engine: its terminals are throttle, an input taking a ratio, which must be joined; force, in N; and flow, the fuel it burns, in kg/s. Its fuel running out is an event, foreseen.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

thrust.description: Its thrust at full throttle, written with its unit: `4500 N`.

isp.description: Its specific impulse, as a length of time: `311 s`.

fuel.description: The fuel it starts with, written with its unit: `100 kg`.

body.description: A body: its terminals are force, in N, and flow, in kg/s, each the sum of what is joined to it; altitude, in m; velocity, in m/s; and contact, a decision asserted on the ground. Reaching the ground is an event, found ahead of time.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

mass.description: Its mass at the start, fuel and all, written with its unit: `1500 kg`.

gravity.description: The gravity it falls in, written with its unit: `1.62 m/s2`.

altitude.description: How high it starts, written with its unit: `500 m`. Not below nought.

velocity.description: How fast it starts, up more than nought, written with its unit: `-20 m/s`.
